name: Question 7
problem: A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, $40%$ are model ${C}_{1},$  $35%$ are model ${C}_{2},$ and the remaining cars are model ${C}_{3}.$ If $6%$ of the model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of the model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the model ${C}_{3}$ cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?
worked_solution:
Let $B$ be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and 

- let ${C}_{1}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{1},$

- let ${C}_{2}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{2},$

- let ${C}_{3}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{3}.$

Then the disjoint union ${C}_{1}⊔{C}_{2}⊔{C}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B\cap {C}_{1})+P(B\cap {C}_{2})+P(B\cap {C}_{3}) \\  & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $40%$ of the cars produced by the company are model ${C}_{1},$ and $50%$ are model ${C}_{2},$  the model ${C}_{3}$ cars make up the remaining

$$
100%-(40%+35%)=25%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P({C}_{1})=0.4,\,P({C}_{2})=0.35,\,P({C}_{3})=0.25.
$$

- Since $6%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of those of model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{3}$ break down during the first year, we have

$$
P(B|{C}_{1})=0.06,\,P(B|{C}_{2})=0.04,\,P(B|{C}_{3})=0.02.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3}) \\  & =(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25) \\  & =0.024+0.014+0.005 \\  & =0.043.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, 40% are model C1, 35% are model C2, and the remaining cars are model C3. If 6% of the model C1, 4% of the model C2, and 2% of the model C3 cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?

a
0.043
b
0.342
c
0.051
d
0.041
e
0.65
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let B be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and

  • let C1 be the event that the car is of model C1,

  • let C2 be the event that the car is of model C2,

  • let C3 be the event that the car is of model C3.

Then the disjoint union C1⊔C2⊔C3 covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability:

P(B)=P(B∩C1)+P(B∩C2)+P(B∩C3)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since 40% of the cars produced by the company are model C1, and 50% are model C2, the model C3 cars make up the remaining 100%−(40%+35%)=25%. As a result, we have P(C1)=0.4,P(C2)=0.35,P(C3)=0.25.

  • Since 6% of the cars of model C1, 4% of those of model C2, and 2% of the cars of model C3 break down during the first year, we have P(B|C1)=0.06,P(B|C2)=0.04,P(B|C3)=0.02.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is

P(B)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)=(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25)=0.024+0.014+0.005=0.043.
